title: "P4 exercises — Signals, growth and reproduction"

The questions follow the [tutorial](index.qmd) and [slides](lec.qmd). Answer
each question before opening its answer.

## Plant hormones

### 1.1

Match each hormone to the effect that best describes it: auxin, cytokinin,
gibberellin, abscisic acid (ABA), ethylene, brassinosteroid.

| | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| A | A gas that promotes ripening of climacteric fruits and leaf abscission |
| B | Promotes cell division in shoot meristems and delays leaf senescence |
| C | Promotes stomatal closure during drought and maintains seed dormancy |
| D | Promotes stem elongation (bolting) and breaks seed dormancy |
| E | Moves by polar transport from the shoot tip; maintains apical dominance and promotes root formation on cuttings |
| F | A steroid that promotes cell expansion; deficient mutants are dark-green dwarfs |

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

A: ethylene. B: cytokinin. C: ABA. D: gibberellin. E: auxin.
F: brassinosteroid.
:::

### 1.2

Predict whether the lateral buds of a pea shoot grow out or stay inhibited
after each treatment.

a. intact plant
b. shoot apex removed (decapitated)
c. shoot apex removed and auxin (IAA) in lanolin paste applied to the cut stump
d. shoot apex removed and plain lanolin applied to the cut stump
e. intact plant with cytokinin applied directly to a lateral bud

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

a. Inhibited. b. Grow out. c. Inhibited: auxin replaces the apex.
d. Grow out: lanolin alone has no effect. e. Grows out: cytokinin promotes
bud outgrowth.

Auxin moving down the stem does not enter the bud. It acts indirectly, by
lowering cytokinin supply to the bud and raising strigolactone synthesis.
:::

### 1.3

Put the steps of starch mobilisation in a germinating barley grain in order.

a. α-amylase is secreted into the starchy endosperm
b. the embryo releases gibberellin
c. sugars are absorbed by the scutellum and supply the growing embryo
d. gibberellin reaches the aleurone layer and induces α-amylase gene expression
e. starch is hydrolysed to sugars

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

b → d → a → e → c. ABA antagonises this response by inhibiting the
gibberellin-induced expression of α-amylase.
:::

### 1.4

Two dwarf pea mutants are sprayed with gibberellin. Mutant A grows to normal
height. Mutant B stays dwarf. Which mutant is most likely defective in
gibberellin biosynthesis, and which in gibberellin perception or signalling?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

Mutant A: biosynthesis. The added hormone replaces what the plant cannot make.
Mutant B: perception or signalling. The plant cannot respond to the hormone
even when it is supplied.
:::

### 1.5

Etiolated (dark-grown) Arabidopsis seedlings are exposed to ethylene.

a. Name the three features of the *triple response*.
b. What do ethylene-treated seedlings of the ethylene-insensitive mutant
   *etr1* look like?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

a. Shorter hypocotyl (and root), thicker (radially swollen) hypocotyl, and
   an exaggerated apical hook.
b. Like untreated dark-grown seedlings: long, thin hypocotyls with a normal
   apical hook. The ETR1 receptor cannot pass on the ethylene signal.
:::

## Tropisms

### 2.1

A coleoptile is lit from one side with blue light. Complete the sentences.

a. The light is detected by the photoreceptor ______.
b. Auxin is redistributed towards the ______ side.
c. Cells on the ______ side elongate faster.
d. The coleoptile therefore bends ______ the light.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

a. Phototropin. b. Shaded. c. Shaded. d. Towards.

This is the Cholodny–Went model: lateral auxin transport causes unequal
growth on the two sides of the organ.
:::

### 2.2

Grass coleoptiles are lit from one side after each treatment. Predict whether
each coleoptile bends towards the light.

a. untreated
b. tip removed
c. tip covered with an opaque cap
d. tip covered with a transparent cap
e. opaque collar around the region below the tip, tip exposed
f. tip cut off and replaced on a thin gelatin block

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

a. Bends. b. No bending. c. No bending. d. Bends. e. Bends. f. Bends.

The light is perceived at the tip, and a signal that can diffuse through
gelatin (auxin) moves down to the growing region below.
:::

### 2.3

A vertically growing root is turned horizontal.

a. Which cells perceive gravity, and which organelles act as statoliths?
b. On which side does auxin accumulate?
c. Which side elongates faster, and in which direction does the root bend?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

a. Columella cells of the root cap. Starch-filled amyloplasts sediment to the
   lower side of the cell.
b. The lower side.
c. The upper side elongates faster, because high auxin concentrations inhibit
   elongation in roots. The root bends downwards.
:::

## Light signalling

### 3.1

Complete the table for phytochrome.

| | Pr | Pfr |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Absorption maximum (colour and approximate wavelength) | | |
| Converted to | | |
| Biologically active form? | | |
| Form in which phytochrome is synthesised? | | |

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

| | Pr | Pfr |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Absorption maximum (colour and approximate wavelength) | Red, about 660 nm | Far-red, about 730 nm |
| Converted to | Pfr | Pr |
| Biologically active form? | No | Yes |
| Form in which phytochrome is synthesised? | Yes | No |
:::

### 3.2

Imbibed lettuce seeds are given brief flashes of red (R) and far-red (FR)
light and then kept in the dark. Predict whether most seeds germinate.

a. dark only
b. R
c. R → FR
d. R → FR → R
e. R → FR → R → FR
f. R → FR → R → FR → R

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

a. No. b. Yes. c. No. d. Yes. e. No. f. Yes.

The last flash decides the outcome. Red light leaves phytochrome mainly as
Pfr, which promotes germination. Far-red light converts it back to Pr.
:::

### 3.3

A seedling grows under a dense leaf canopy.

a. Is the red : far-red ratio higher or lower than in direct sunlight? Why?
b. How does this change the proportion of phytochrome in the Pfr form?
c. Name two shade-avoidance responses.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

a. Lower. Chlorophyll absorbs red light but transmits and reflects far-red
   light.
b. The proportion of Pfr falls.
c. Any two of: faster stem and petiole elongation, upward leaf movement,
   reduced branching, earlier flowering.
:::

### 3.4

Match each photoreceptor to the light it absorbs and to one response it
controls: phytochrome, cryptochrome, phototropin, UVR8.

Light: blue/UV-A; blue/UV-A; red/far-red; UV-B.

Responses: phototropism and chloroplast movement; seed germination and shade
avoidance; inhibition of hypocotyl elongation and entrainment of the
circadian clock; UV-protective responses.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

| Photoreceptor | Light | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Phytochrome | Red/far-red | Seed germination and shade avoidance |
| Cryptochrome | Blue/UV-A | Inhibition of hypocotyl elongation; circadian clock entrainment |
| Phototropin | Blue/UV-A | Phototropism and chloroplast movement (also stomatal opening) |
| UVR8 | UV-B | UV-protective responses |
:::

## Germination and dormancy

### 4.1

Classify each seed as dormant or quiescent.

a. Dry seeds stored in a packet.
b. Freshly harvested seeds do not germinate on moist paper at 20 °C, but do
   after several months of dry storage.
c. Seeds in dry soil germinate after the first rain.
d. Seeds germinate only after several weeks of moist chilling.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

a. Quiescent. b. Dormant (released by after-ripening). c. Quiescent.
d. Dormant (released by cold stratification).
:::

### 4.2

Predict the germination behaviour of:

a. an ABA-deficient mutant
b. a gibberellin-deficient mutant

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

a. Reduced dormancy. Seeds may germinate while still on the mother plant
   (vivipary).
b. Seeds fail to germinate unless gibberellin is supplied.

The ABA : gibberellin balance regulates dormancy: ABA maintains it, and
gibberellin promotes germination.
:::

### 4.3

Four dishes each contain 20 seeds. By day 5, radicles have emerged from 12
and 14 seeds in the two control dishes, and from 16 and 18 seeds in the two
treated dishes. Calculate the germination percentage of each dish and the
mean for each group.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

Control: 60% and 70%, mean 65%. Treated: 80% and 90%, mean 85%.
:::

## Flowering and reproduction

### 5.1

A short-day plant (SDP) and a long-day plant (LDP) both have a critical night
length of 11 h. Predict whether each plant flowers under each 24 h cycle.

a. 16 h light / 8 h dark
b. 8 h light / 16 h dark
c. 8 h light / 16 h dark, with the night interrupted in the middle by a brief red flash
d. as c, but the red flash is followed immediately by a far-red flash
e. 8 h light / 16 h dark, with the light period interrupted by 1 h of darkness

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

| | SDP | LDP |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a | No | Yes |
| b | Yes | No |
| c | No | Yes |
| d | Yes | No |
| e | Yes | No |

The length of the uninterrupted night is the deciding factor. A red night
break divides the long night into two short ones. Far-red reverses the red
effect, so phytochrome perceives the night break. Darkness during the day has
no effect.
:::

### 5.2

In Arabidopsis under long days, name:

a. the organ that perceives the photoperiod
b. the mobile protein that signals floral induction
c. the tissue through which it moves
d. the site where it acts to start flower formation

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

a. Leaves. b. FLOWERING LOCUS T (FT). c. Phloem. d. Shoot apical meristem,
where FT with the transcription factor FD activates floral meristem identity
genes.
:::

### 5.3

True or false? Correct any false statements.

a. Vernalisation makes a plant flower while it is still in the cold.
b. Vernalisation is perceived by the shoot apex.
c. In Arabidopsis, vernalisation represses the flowering repressor *FLC*.
d. The vernalised state is passed on to the plant's seeds.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

a. False. Prolonged cold gives the competence to flower. Flowering itself
   usually happens later, under warmer, inductive conditions.
b. True.
c. True. *FLC* stays repressed through later cell divisions after the cold.
d. False. The vernalised state is reset in each generation, so the offspring
   need cold again.
:::

### 5.4

Complete the table for double fertilisation in a typical angiosperm.

| Structure | Formed from | Ploidy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Zygote | | |
| Endosperm | | |
| Seed coat | | |
| Fruit wall (pericarp) | | |

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

| Structure | Formed from | Ploidy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Zygote | One sperm cell + egg cell | 2n |
| Endosperm | Second sperm cell + central cell (two polar nuclei) | 3n |
| Seed coat | Integuments of the ovule (maternal) | 2n |
| Fruit wall (pericarp) | Ovary wall (maternal) | 2n |
:::

## Senescence

### 6.1

a. Name the hormone that delays leaf senescence and two hormones that promote it.
b. Which of these nutrients are efficiently remobilised from a senescing leaf
   to the seeds: nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, calcium?
c. Through which tissue are remobilised nutrients exported from the leaf?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

a. Cytokinin delays senescence. Ethylene, ABA and jasmonic acid promote it
   (any two).
b. Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium. Calcium is immobile in the phloem and
   stays in the leaf.
c. Phloem.
:::
